title: Imperatives and Negative Commands
lede: Derive and use commands for singular, dual and plural addressees, and form accurate prohibitions with لا الناهية and the jussive.

items.prompt: Choose the command “Write!” to one male.
items.feedback: The masculine singular imperative is اُكْتُبْ.
The feminine singular command takes ـي.

items.prompt: Choose “Do not write!” to one male.
Choose “Do not write!” to one female.
items.feedback: The nūn drops in the jussive five-verb form.
Politeness can be added without changing the core command grammar.

options: guess the opening vowel every time

items.feedback: Dual imperative; the hamza spelling contracts with alif.

items.prompt: Which is future negation, not prohibition?
Best polite request to one female
Best road prohibition to a group

blocks: ## Why this matters لِمَاذَا نَحْتَاجُ إِلَى الْأَمْرِ وَالنَّهْيِ؟
Commands and prohibitions appear in role plays, signs, directions, recipes, instructions and everyday requests.
Use core masculine and feminine singular commands.
Control dual, masculine/mixed plural and feminine plural commands and prohibitions.
Explain derivation from the jussive and choose a suitable tone or formal alternative.
[callout] Communication target: Give clear, polite instructions that another person can follow successfully.
The imperative is based on second-person present/jussive forms, not on the English command.
[callout] Derivation route: Start from the second-person jussive present, remove the prefix تـ , then add a helping vowel if the word would begin with a difficult consonant cluster.

TABLE: Step | كَتَبَ / يَكْتُبُ | دَرَسَ / يَدْرُسُ | جَلَسَ / يَجْلِسُ // 2nd person present | تَكْتُبُ | تَدْرُسُ | تَجْلِسُ // jussive base | تَكْتُبْ | تَدْرُسْ | تَجْلِسْ // remove تـ | كْتُبْ | دْرُسْ | جْلِسْ // imperative | اُكْتُبْ | اُدْرُسْ | اِجْلِسْ
[callout/warning] Helping vowel: The initial vowel is not always the same. Learn common imperatives with their present pair: يَكْتُبُ / اُكْتُبْ، يَدْرُسُ / اُدْرُسْ، يَجْلِسُ / اِجْلِسْ .
The command stem combines with a small, reusable ending family.

TABLE: Addressee | كَتَبَ | ذَهَبَ | قَرَأَ // أَنْتَ | اُكْتُبْ | اِذْهَبْ | اِقْرَأْ // أَنْتِ | اُكْتُبِي | اِذْهَبِي | اِقْرَئِي // أَنْتُمَا | اُكْتُبَا | اِذْهَبَا | اِقْرَآ // أَنْتُمْ | اُكْتُبُوا | اِذْهَبُوا | اِقْرَؤُوا // أَنْتُنَّ | اُكْتُبْنَ | اِذْهَبْنَ | اِقْرَأْنَ
[callout] Commands have an audience. Choose the ending according to one male, one female, two people, a masculine/mixed group or a feminine group.
A prohibition tells the addressee not to perform an action.

TABLE: Positive command | Negative prohibition | Meaning // اُكْتُبْ | لَا تَكْتُبْ | write / do not write (m.s.) // اُكْتُبِي | لَا تَكْتُبِي | write / do not write (f.s.) // اُكْتُبَا | لَا تَكْتُبَا | write / do not write (dual) // اُكْتُبُوا | لَا تَكْتُبُوا | write / do not write (m./mixed pl.) // اُكْتُبْنَ | لَا تَكْتُبْنَ | write / do not write (f. pl.)
[callout] Different structures: Positive commands use the imperative. Negative commands use لَا النَّاهِيَةُ followed by a jussive second-person present form.
Instructions, directions, recipes, notices and role plays require both accurate form and appropriate tone.
مِنْ فَضْلِكِ، اِقْرَئِي النَّصَّ بِصَوْتٍ وَاضِحٍ.
Useful alternative when no direct addressee is foregrounded.
[callout] Tone matters: Add مِنْ فَضْلِكَ / مِنْ فَضْلِكِ , a greeting or a reason when a direct command could sound abrupt.
A useful correction explains the form, not only the answer.
The command is derived from the present/jussive, not the past base.
لن states future negation; لا الناهية gives a negative command.
Grammar becomes useful when it helps you understand and communicate.
Read signs, recipes and digital instructions. Classify each as positive command, prohibition or impersonal formal request.
Follow a partner’s route or drawing instructions, then identify whether each command addressed one person or a group.
Perform a role play giving directions or explaining a process. Add polite openings and clarification questions.
Repair instructions with past forms used as commands, wrong addressee endings and retained nūn after prohibitive لا.
Create a 12-step Arabic guide for a school activity, recipe, journey or digital task. Include at least three negative instructions and vary the addressee in a short second section.
[callout] Model: أَوَّلًا، اِفْتَحْ الْمِلَفَّ. بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ اُكْتُبْ عُنْوَانَكَ. لَا تَنْسَ أَنْ تَحْفَظَ الْعَمَلَ، وَلَا تُغْلِقِ الْمُتَصَفِّحَ قَبْلَ الْحِفْظِ.
[callout] Success checklist: Use accurate opening vowels, at least one feminine command, one group command, three prohibitions and polite language where appropriate.
Plan the verb changes as a timeline, root map or sentence flowchart. Label each form in Arabic.
Write the instructions as numbered steps. Underline positive imperatives once and negative prohibitions twice.
Choose the correct command and prohibition forms.
- select endings for singular, dual and plural addressees;
- form prohibitions with لا الناهية and the jussive;
- use direct and polite instructions in practical contexts.
Return in 3–7 days and repeat the final check without reviewing first. Retrieval, not recognition alone, builds secure verb control.
